one_liner: Header-only C++ template-metaprogramming regex engine for compile-time-known patterns, with large wall-clock wins over std::regex.
what_it_does: CTRE compiles PCRE-like regex patterns into specialized C++ template code at compile time, so matching, searching, and capturing require no runtime pattern-parsing step. The pattern is supplied as a compile-time string (`ctre::match<"pattern">(subject)` in C++20, or a `ctll::fixed_string` constexpr in C++17), not a runtime std::string, so it is not a drop-in for std::regex call sites. Results come back as a `regex_results` object deconstructible via structured bindings rather than std::smatch, and the library also exposes search/starts_with/range/tokenize/split entry points plus named and numbered captures.
how_it_is_fast: Regex parsing and construction of the matching logic both happen at compile time via constexpr functions and template metaprogramming (the bundled ctll parser), so the compiler emits specialized branch/comparison code for one exact pattern instead of interpreting a generic runtime NFA the way std::regex does. This removes std::regex's per-call pattern-compilation cost entirely and lets ordinary compiler optimizations (inlining, constant folding) act directly on the matcher. The tradeoff is longer compile times and larger generated code in exchange for eliminated runtime interpretation overhead.
when_to_use: Pattern is a compile-time literal or constexpr reused across many match calls (parsers, lexers, validators), not built from runtime user input.
Hot-path matching/parsing where std::regex's per-invocation compile step dominates runtime.
Want structured-binding capture access (e.g. `auto [whole, year, month] = ...`) instead of std::smatch/std::ssub_match.
Project can require clang 14+, gcc 9+, or MSVC 16.11+ and build with C++17/20.
Header-only vendoring is acceptable — a single-header variant exists for easy drop-in as a source file.
when_not_to_use: Pattern arrives at runtime (user-supplied, config-loaded) — CTRE patterns must be compile-time-known, so it can't replace std::regex there.
Need PCRE features CTRE excludes: callouts, comments, conditional patterns, \cX control-char escapes, \K match-point reset, named characters, octal numbers, subroutines, \X grapheme clusters.
Taking the README's or bench files' >50x numbers at face value: they are tier-C, dated 2018-10-23, with no CPU, compiler version, flags, or input size stated.
Correctness on edge cases matters as much as speed: open bugs include incorrect matches with repeated capture groups (#300) and lookahead failing to compile with UTF-8 input (#338).

integration.dependencies: none (bundles its own ctll template-parser headers)
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 (C++20 for the `<pattern>` NTTP syntax); clang 14+, gcc 9+, MSVC 16.11+ (VS 2019 16.11)
integration.platforms: any (portable standard C++, no architecture-specific code)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same match/search/capture concepts as std::regex, but the pattern must be a compile-time template argument (not a runtime std::string) and results are a regex_results/structured-binding type rather than std::smatch, so call sites need rewriting

gotchas: Pattern must be compile-time-known: a template argument or constexpr ctll::fixed_string, never something assembled at runtime.
The N3599 UDL syntax (`"regex"_ctre`) on GCC 9.1+ requires defining CTRE_ENABLE_LITERALS and building without -pedantic.
Unicode support is opt-in via separate `<ctre-unicode.hpp>` + `<unicode-db.hpp>` includes; omitting them gives missing-symbol link errors, not silent fallback.
Open bugs: incorrect match with repeated capture groups (#300, 2025), lookahead fails to compile with UTF-8 strings (#338, 2025), MSVC internal compiler error on some inputs (#255, 2022).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick CTRE over RE2 when the pattern set is fixed at compile time and you want zero runtime regex-compile overhead with PCRE-like syntax and structured-binding captures; pick RE2 instead when patterns are supplied at runtime or you need its linear-time worst-case guarantee against untrusted/adversarial input.
verified_claims_summary: First-party `time`-command runs (clang-bench.txt and gcc-bench.txt, committed 2018-10-23) show CTRE beating std::regex by roughly 11x-125x wall-clock across four patterns under clang (e.g. 10.093s vs 21m9.309s on 'ABCD|DEFGH|EFGHI|A{4,}') and roughly 14x-24x under gcc (e.g. 3.982s vs 0m55.058s on the same pattern), with no compiler version, optimization flags, CPU, or input size recorded. A separate WG21 P1433R0 table gives CTRE 3.172s vs std::regex/libstdc++ 33.585s on Linux/gcc and CTRE 11.11s vs std::regex/libc++ 1655s on macOS/clang, and that macOS figure duplicates a clang-bench.txt number exactly, so the two sources' data provenance is unclear.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-09-11, CMakeLists reports v3.11.0) with 3.9k stars and used as the reference implementation for WG21 proposal P1433; Apache-2.0 licensed and header-only, so cheap to vendor even though its headline benchmark numbers are old (2018) and thinly documented.
